title: Hardened Seat and Anti-Rotation Feature for the Trim Air Pressure Regulating Valve

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: First answer to trim air valve seat erosion, introducing a hardened seat and a keyed anti-rotation feature so that the valve holds its commanded position instead of drifting towards the cold stop during long cruise segments.

sections.reason: Cabin zone temperature complaints traced to trim air valves that no longer hold position accounted for eleven per cent of all cabin write-ups reported in 2015 across a tracked population of two hundred and ninety aircraft. Teardown of forty returned valves showed the same picture in every case: erosion of the soft seat by the hot trim air, followed by rotation of the seat carrier inside its housing, after which the valve authority collapsed and the zone drifted towards whatever the pack was delivering. Operators were replacing valves at roughly a third of the published mean time between unscheduled removals and the spares pool could not keep up.
sections.description: The modification replaces the soft valve seat by a cobalt-faced hardened seat carrier and adds a machined key that locates the carrier against rotation in the housing. The regulator body ASH878362-87 is retained but the internal seat stack is new, and the inlet filter KAD437362-51 is changed to a coarser mesh that no longer blinds when the seat material sheds. The cover screws are changed to AES731670-69 with a revised torque figure because the new carrier is stiffer and the old figure was distorting the flange. The valve at FIN 726HQ in the forward distribution run and the valve at FIN 980HQ in the aft run are both modified; no ducting is changed and no bracketry moves. Work is done in zones 254 and 291 through the existing ceiling access. Detail is on drawing D21601117401.
sections.effects: Mass increase of 0.9 kilograms per aircraft with no measurable effect on balance. No electrical load change. The modified valve is one way interchangeable: a modified valve may be fitted to an unmodified aircraft but the original valve must not be fitted back into a modified installation because the housing key slot is machined at embodiment. Mean time between unscheduled removals is expected to improve by a factor of three. The trim air section of the maintenance manual and the parts figure both require revision, and the coarser filter changes the cleaning interval published for the zone.
sections.embodiment_note: Production cut-in at MSN Z05436 in April 2016. Retrofit is by service bulletin during any line maintenance opportunity of four hours or more; the ceiling panels in the affected zone must come down but the cabin does not have to be stripped. Kits were available from the third quarter of 2016.

type_data.production_impact: Cut-in at MSN Z05436, absorbed in the normal valve supply
